Description

The --help output of gh search issues and gh search prs lacked information on using boolean operators (OR, AND) and parentheses for nesting.

For the operators to work, they must be passed as separate argument, rather than inside a multi-word quoted sting (in which case they get interpreted as plain words), otherwise and the search can omit relevant results (or return nothing at all) without signaling usage of unsupported syntax.

I decided to contribute this info to the --help output of those commands, so that others (and my future self! 😅) could know how to proceed in case they bump into this issue.

How did you test this change?

This change only affects help text; no behavior is changed. I verified that the output matches the expected by checking the rendered help output:

  • go run ./cmd/gh search issues --help
  • go run ./cmd/gh search prs --help

Just to be sure, I also confirmed that the relevant tests still pass, with go test ./pkg/cmd/search/issues/ ./pkg/cmd/search/prs/.

Authorship and follow-up

Who wrote this:

  • A human wrote it.
  • An agent wrote it under close human direction.
  • An agent wrote it independently, and no human has guided the implementation beyond the initial prompt.

Who answers review comments:

  • @username will read and reply directly. Name the account.
  • An agent will draft replies and @username will read them before they are posted.
  • Nobody has explicitly committed to replying.

Note: I used an AI agent to help with troubleshooting the original issue, but I authored the change, commit message and this PR description myself.

feat(cli): read other reviewers' feedback at capture (#53)
df45f75 
Refs PLAT-494. The CI reviewer repeats findings that another reviewer
already raised, because loupe reads back only its own earlier round.
`loupe capture` now also reads the pull request's existing feedback.
That is submitted reviews, inline review threads and top-level comments,
each read to its last page. It stores them in the run as
`comments.json`. `loupe show --comments [--json]` hands them to the
agent offline, the same way `--previous` does. Spec:
`specs/029-reviewer-comments/`.

- **Self-exclusion.** A review is left out only when it is a loupe
review whose `src=` name, version aside, matches `--source`, and whose
author passes the sticky publisher rule. The author is the viewer for a
user token, or a `[bot]` for an installation token. So two people on the
same skill do not hide each other, and the rule never excludes on login
alone. The rule is split out of `newestOwn`, not copied. Its comments in
threads are dropped, and everyone's replies to them stay.
- **Threads over GraphQL.** REST has no resolved state. The client
follows both cursors, the threads and each thread's comments. It names a
bot `name[bot]` as REST does, and it links a comment to its review by
`fullDatabaseId`, because `databaseId` is deprecated.
- **A failed read is a reason, never an empty list.** Any listing that
fails, a later page included, stores only a reason. `show --comments`
then refuses `not-found` and carries it. The capture itself never
refuses.
- **Contract change.** `contracts/cli.md` gains capture's `comments` key
and `show --comments`. Capture now lists the reviews once and shares
that list with the `--previous` read. With a local receipt, a round
therefore makes one review request instead of none. That amends spec
027's US3 AS1 and SC-004, and it is recorded in the spec and in the
plan's Complexity Tracking.
- The `human-review` skill reads `show --comments` next to `--previous`,
and says the bodies are untrusted data.
- Test support: `fakegh` serves GraphQL threads and issue comments.
`SetPageSize` caps pages, `FailAfter` fails a later page, and
`Request.Read()` tells a GraphQL query from a write.

## Checks

`GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false mise run check` after the last commit printed
`0 issues.`, and every package was `ok`, `internal/integration` included
(100.9s). A plain `mise run check` fails on this machine with `error
obtaining VCS status`, because a stray non-repository `~/.git` sits in
the home directory. The pre-commit hook passed on every commit, since
git sets `GIT_DIR`.

Each guard was confirmed by mutation. Each broken guard failed only its
intended tests:

| Mutation | Caught by |
| :--- | :--- |
| drop the `src=` match |
`TestReadCommentsLeavesOutThePublishersOwnReviews/{another_bot_source,
the_viewer's_own_on_another_source}` |
| drop the author rule | `…/{a_person_on_the_same_source,_unattended,
someone_else_on_the_same_source}` |
| drop `IsLoupe` (shared) | `…/{the_viewer's_own,_not_loupe,
a_bot's,_not_loupe}`, `TestFindSticky` |
| list `PENDING` / keep emptied threads / keep own thread comments |
`TestReadCommentsKeepsOthersRepliesInOwnThreads` |
| store a failure as empty lists |
`TestReadCommentsFailureIsAReasonNotAnEmptyList` (all 5 cases) |
| REST, threads, or thread comments stop after page 1 | the client,
fakegh and publish cross-page tests |
| drop resolved, outdated, or the `[bot]` suffix |
`TestListReviewThreadsFollowsBothCursors` and the two cross-page tests |
| `show --comments` answers a failed read |
`TestShowCommentsRefusesWithoutFeedback/a_failed_read`,
`TestCaptureSurvivesAFailedFeedbackRead` |
| capture drops `--source` from the exclusion |
`TestCIRoundReadsOtherReviewersButNotItsOwn` |

The threads query and the thread-comments continuation were run
read-only against `cli/cli#14519` and `#14509`. Both validate, and
`fullDatabaseId` comes back as a digit string. Two read-only reviews ran
on another model: the first found the `databaseId` deprecation, and the
second found no defect in the fix.

## Not verified

- A live capture against a real pull request. In particular, nothing
here shows that an installation token can read review threads and issue
comments. Only the query shape was checked live.
- The checks in `specs/001-loupe-v1/validation.md`'s Unverified list.

Follow-up outside this repository: once released, github-actions-library
needs its loupe version bumped in `actions/loupe-capture`, and a prompt
rule that reads `loupe show --comments --json`.

Refuse a merge the wrapper cannot see, and test both copies of merge-…
dfdbc00 
…pr.mjs (#209)

Closes #200

Both copies of `merge-pr.mjs` now have tests, and the shipped copy no
longer merges when it cannot tell whether a branch is behind its base.
ADR 0063 records the decision, and which of the remaining differences
between the copies are configuration and which are behaviour.

## Functionality

**What the premise got right, and where it went further.** The fail-open
was real, and it had three causes, not one:

1. **Every fork PR.** The compare asked about the head by branch *name*,
which a fork's branch does not have in the base repository. I measured
this on a public fork PR, cli/cli#14519:
`compare/trunk...document-search-operator-support` returned **404**,
`compare/trunk...<headRefOid>` returned **0**, and
`compare/trunk...waldyrious:<branch>` returned **0**. Under the old
code, every fork PR skipped the refusal.
2. **Any `gh` error.**
3. **An empty answer.** `Number('')` is `0`, so an empty answer read as
"not behind" and got past the `NaN` test.

It also turned up a fork defect the issue did not name. After a merge
the wrapper runs `DELETE refs/heads/<headRefName>` in the *base*
repository. For a fork PR opened from the fork's own `main`, that
deletes the base repository's `main` wherever nothing protects it, which
is the setup the asset is written for.

**Decision on a null lookup: refuse** (while `REFUSE_WHEN_BEHIND` is
on). The refusal prints the `gh` error and the exact `gh api` call, so
the operator can rerun it by hand. Asking by head SHA is what keeps this
from costing fork PRs every merge. The remaining cost falls on the
maintainer: a dead token, no network or a rate limit is now a hard stop
instead of a warning. Only a public fork was measured.

**What I ran:**

- `node --test scripts/merge-pr.test.mjs`: 58 tests, all passing. The
shared suite runs 27 cases against each copy, and 4 more are
copy-specific.
- **Mutation check.** I put each of the four defects back into the
asset, one at a time, and reran the suite. Each one turned it red:
fail-open on null (9 tests), compare by name (5), deleting a fork's
branch (3), and an empty answer read as 0 (3).
- `node scripts/merge-pr.mjs` with no argument prints usage and exits 1.
`node scripts/merge-pr.mjs 207` refused with "state is MERGED" and exit
1.
- **Read-only dry run of the real module against real `gh`, with `PUT`
and `DELETE` intercepted.** Results are in the comment below.
- `npm run check` is green, with 990 tests. `check:plugin` and
`check:plugin-load` are green, and `check:version` reports 0.54.5 →
0.54.6 (rebased onto #208, which took 0.54.5 and ADR 0062, so this ADR
is 0063).

**Not done:** I did not open an interactive `claude --plugin-dir .`
session. The skill change is one paragraph in
`references/enforcement.md`, layer 1, and I read it in the file.

## Code

`run({ prNumber, gh, sleep, log, warn, error, required, refuseWhenBehind
})` returns an exit code instead of calling `process.exit`. The
entry-point check is the same one `post-body.mjs` uses. The body is
identical in both copies, except for three things:

- `REQUIRED`'s values
- comments
- this repository's WHAT JUST SHIPPED block

`REQUIRED` stays a column-0 `const` because `check-setup.mjs` reads it
with `^const REQUIRED = \[`.

The two copies used to differ in about 60 lines of code. Now they differ
in the `REQUIRED` line and the release block, and nothing else.

The `staleRefusal` message adds the HTTP 405 sentence only when GitHub
reports `BEHIND`, which is the one case where that sentence is true.

## Architecture

- **No new pattern.** The injected-`gh`, importable shape is taken from
`post-body.mjs`. One test file covering two copies follows the precedent
of `command-reader.test.mjs`.
- **New ADR 0063.** It holds the null decision, the SHA compare, the
fork-delete fix, and a table that sorts every remaining difference into
configuration, behaviour or prose.
- **This repository's copy gains `REFUSE_WHEN_BEHIND = true`.** Here it
is redundant with the ruleset, and deliberately so: it is the only place
the logic gets exercised before a stranger trusts it.
- **Payload changed:** the asset and `references/enforcement.md`. The
version goes to 0.54.6, as briefed.
- **Out of scope, left alone:** the guard files, and #205.

Document search operator support in gh search help
97577e4 
The `--help` output of `gh search issues` and `gh search prs`
lacked information on using boolean operators (`OR`, `AND`)
and parentheses for nesting. Each operator must be passed as separate arguments;
wrapping a whole query string in quotes makes it match as a single literal phrase,
so the operators are treated as plain words,
and the search will fail to capture relevant results
rather than reporting usage of unsupported syntax.

This patch updates the help text to make this nuance explicit to users.
